dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談員です。最初に年齢、性別をお聞かせください。
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm the counselor. To begin, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: こんにちは31歳、女性です
dialogue.English: Hello. I’m a 31-year-old woman.

dialogue.content: 本日はどのようなご相談ですか？
dialogue.English: What would you like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: 毎日子どもに怒ってばかりで疲れてしまいます
dialogue.English: I end up getting angry at my children every day, and I’m exhausted.

dialogue.content: お子さんをつい叱ってしまうのですね？
dialogue.English: So, you find yourself scolding your children unintentionally?

dialogue.content: そうなんです。毎日いっぱいいっぱいで
dialogue.English: That's right. I feel so overwhelmed every day.

dialogue.content: なるほど。お子さんはおいくつですか？
dialogue.English: I see. How old are your children?

dialogue.content: 10時と8歳です
dialogue.English: They’re 10 and 8 years old.
I mean, 10 years old.

dialogue.content: お二人だと、なお大変ですよね
dialogue.English: Having two must be even more challenging, isn't it?

dialogue.content: そうですね。先日下の男の子がお友達の物を壊したと学校から連絡が来たんです
dialogue.English: Yes. The other day, the school contacted me saying my younger son broke a friend's belonging.

dialogue.content: 人に迷惑をかけて欲しくないし、人の痛み、気持ちをわかって行動して欲しいです
dialogue.English: I don't want him to cause trouble for others, and I want him to understand people's pain and feelings and act accordingly.

dialogue.content: なるほど。元気なお年頃ですからね。
dialogue.English: I see. They're at an energetic age, after all.

dialogue.content: しかし、人に迷惑をかけてしまうことが心配ですよね？
dialogue.English: But you're worried about him causing trouble for others, right?

dialogue.content: そうなんです！人に迷惑をかけて欲しくないんです。特定の子にたまに叩いていることもあったみたいです
dialogue.English: Exactly! I really don't want him to bother others. It seems he has also hit a particular child at times.

dialogue.content: それで学校と相手の親の方と面談がありました
dialogue.English: So I had a meeting with the school and the other child’s parents.

dialogue.content: 叩いてしまうということは、相手のお子さんも傷ついてしまいますし、なお心配になりますよね。
dialogue.English: The hitting must hurt the other child, which would make you even more worried.

dialogue.content: ほんとに相手の子にも親御さんにも申し訳なくて
dialogue.English: I feel truly sorry for both the other child and their parents.

dialogue.content: 話の途中になりますが、お名前は何とお呼びしたらよろしいですか？
dialogue.English: I'm sorry to interrupt, but what would you like me to call you?

dialogue.content: はるでお願いします
dialogue.English: Please call me Haru.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。相手の親御さんとは問題解決できましたか？
dialogue.English: I understand. Were you able to resolve the issue with the other parents?

dialogue.content: とりあえずの問題解決は出来ましたが、申し訳ない気持ちでいっぱいです。うちの子自身も事の重大さをわかってるかどうかも微妙だし...
dialogue.English: We managed to resolve the issue for the time being, but I’m still filled with guilt. I’m not even sure if my child really understands the seriousness of what happened...

dialogue.content: そうですか。はるさんとしても、心痛なされたことと思います。
dialogue.English: I see. That must have been heartbreaking for you as well, Haru.

dialogue.content: それで、ますます叱ってしまうことが増えるとそれも心痛ですしね。
dialogue.English: And then, if you end up scolding him more and more because of this, that's painful for you too.

dialogue.content: そうですね、勉強ももちろん出来て欲しいですが、それよりも人を傷つけない優しい子になって欲しいです
dialogue.English: Yes. Of course I want him to do well in school, but more than that, I want him to be a kind child who doesn’t hurt others.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。やはり心の優しい子になってほしいですよね。ちなみにお子さんがそういった行動をされるようになったのはいつ頃からでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I agree. You want him to grow into a kind-hearted child, don't you? By the way, when did he start showing this kind of behavior?

dialogue.content: 保育園の年中頃にも当時の担任から言葉遣いやお友達に手を出してると言われた事があります
dialogue.English: Around the middle year of preschool, his teacher at the time told me he was using rough language and hitting his friends.

dialogue.content: 私の子育てがいけないのでしょうか
dialogue.English: Is my parenting to blame?

dialogue.content: いえ、それは一概には言い切れないです。上のお子さんは似た傾向がありますか？
dialogue.English: No, we can't necessarily say that. Does your older child have similar tendencies?

dialogue.content: 上の子は兄弟間ではありますが、友達関係ではありません
dialogue.English: My older child does, but only between siblings, not with friends.

dialogue.content: そうですか。では、はるさんの子育てのせいとは言い切れないように思います。
dialogue.English: I see. In that case, it doesn’t seem fair to conclude it’s because of your parenting.

dialogue.content: そうだといいのですが、ありがとうございます
dialogue.English: I hope that's the case. Thank you.

dialogue.content: そう思います。でも、はるさんは𠮟ってしまうことを悩まれていますから、
dialogue.English: I think so. But since you're troubled by the fact that you end up scolding him,

dialogue.content: そこに原因をお考えなのではないですか？
dialogue.English: perhaps you feel that is the cause?

dialogue.content: そうですね、毎日叱ってしまうのが嫌です
dialogue.English: Yes, I hate that I end up scolding him every day.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。叱ることは、お子さんのことを思ってのことなのに、逆に苦しめていると感じることも多いのではないでしょうか。
dialogue.English: I understand. Even though you scold them because you're thinking of their well-being, you might often feel like you're actually causing them pain, don't you?

dialogue.content: 子どもが萎縮して育ってしまうのではないかと思います
dialogue.English: I worry he’ll grow up feeling intimidated and shrinking into himself.

dialogue.content: なるほど。お気持ちよく分かります。お子さんにはのびのびと育ってほしいですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. I completely understand how you feel. You want your children to grow up freely and uninhibited, don't you?

dialogue.content: そうですね、のびのびと育って欲しいです！
dialogue.English: Yes, I want them to grow up freely and uninhibited!

dialogue.content: 家庭が居心地いいところであって欲しい
dialogue.English: I want our home to be a comfortable place for them.

dialogue.content: ですよね。それがはるさんの願いですよね。何かご自身で変化されることを考えておられるのですか？
dialogue.English: Of course. That's your wish, isn't it, Haru? Have you thought about any changes you could make yourself?

dialogue.content: 変化というのは叱らないようになれたらという事ですか？
dialogue.English: By changes, do you mean being able to stop scolding?

dialogue.content: そう考えておられるように感じました。
dialogue.English: That’s how it sounded to me.

dialogue.content: そうですね、叱らずのびのび子育てが出来ることが理想です
dialogue.English: Yes, my ideal is to raise them freely, without scolding.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。のびのび子育てができればそれが理想ですよね。
dialogue.English: That makes sense. Being able to raise them freely would be the ideal, wouldn't it?

dialogue.content: どうしたらもう少し余裕が持てますかね？
dialogue.English: How can I have a bit more composure?

dialogue.content: そうですね。叱る必然のある場面もありますから、
dialogue.English: Well, there are situations where scolding is necessary,

dialogue.content: 叱る必然のないときには叱らないために、余裕を持てればよいですよね。
dialogue.English: so it would be good to have more composure so you don't scold when it isn't needed, right?

dialogue.content: 怒りの沸点が低いんですかね？
dialogue.English: Maybe I just have a low boiling point?

dialogue.content: 怒りの沸点、たしかにそういうことはあるかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: A low boiling point... yes, that might be a factor.

dialogue.content: お子さんを思われるあまりに、ということだから、それもすごく分かりますが。
dialogue.English: But it comes from how much you care about your children, which I completely understand.

dialogue.content: もう少し余裕を持てるように頑張ってみます！
dialogue.English: I'll try to work on having more composure!

dialogue.content: 話しが出来て少し楽になれました
dialogue.English: Talking about it has made me feel a little lighter.

dialogue.content: はい。ありがとうございます。これからも頑張ってくださいね。
dialogue.English: Yes. Thank you. Please keep doing your best.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you, too.
